p01: Every month, lenders send the same reminder, at the same time, to everyone.
p02: Kairos looks at every borrower, every day, and decides.
p03: Before anything goes out, Aladdin, our safety supervisor, checks it against the lender's rules.
p04: No reply on SMS. So it learns, and tries WhatsApp.
p06: But even they can't break the rules.
p07: Kairos answers in seconds. But only once it knows it's really them.
p08: A doctored payment screenshot? It checks with the bank.
p10: In our tests, about twice the money back for every rupee. With zero rule breaches.
t01: This is what happens inside Kairos, for one borrower, on one day.
t02: Everything starts from one record: loans, payments, replies and consent. Money to the paisa.
t03: Each day, a Bayesian learner scores every channel and hour, per segment and per borrower.
t04: Models only suggest. Aladdin reserves the budget and limits, then checks every rule again at send time.
t05: Messages go out through each channel. Delivery and replies come back as webhooks, and duplicates are ignored.
t06: Replies climb a ladder: rules first, then a small model. Thresholds are hand-set, and when it's unsure, it hands off to a person.
t07: People can step in at any moment. Every action still passes Aladdin, and lands in the audit log.
t08: Every outcome feeds the learner. Same data in, same decisions out.
t09: We attack it, load it, and test it.
tv_voice: Voice calls run on Sarvam agents. Every call comes back with a disposition and a confidence. Below a hand-set threshold, a person reviews it.
tv_intent: Replies climb a ladder: rules first, then a small model. Still unsure? A person decides.
tv_proof: Same data in, same decisions out. And we attack it, load it, and test it.
t02b: Each day, every borrower is re-sorted. Every move names its rule.
t03b: A Bayesian learner tracks reply chances. On day seven, WhatsApp replies drop. Kairos isn't told.
t03c: By the end of day fourteen, that segment has moved to SMS. Learned from replies alone.
